questions.question: Most motorcycle crashes happen:

options.text: On short trips.
On long trips.
After at least an hour of riding.
After more than 8 hours of riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: On short trips.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen on trips shorter than five miles, within the first few minutes of riding.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions or hazards.

questions.question: Where is the engine cut-off switch usually located?

options.text: Near the left handgrip
Near the right handgrip
Near the left footrest
Near the right footrest

questions.correctAnswerText: Near the right handgrip
questions.explanation: The engine cut-off switch is located next to the right handgrip. Learn where all your motorcycle controls are before you ride.

questions.question: It is important to flash your brake light when:

options.text: Approaching a police officer.
Someone is following too closely.
There is a stop sign ahead.
Your signals are not working.

questions.correctAnswerText: Someone is following too closely.
questions.explanation: Flash your brake light before slowing down if someone is tailgating you. They may not see the hazard ahead that is causing you to slow. Also flash your brake light if you are slowing in a place where other drivers might not expect it.

questions.question: When approaching a blind intersection, you should:

options.text: Ride in the portion of the lane that will bring you into other drivers' fields of vision at the earliest possible moment.
Always be in the left lane to be the farthest from oncoming traffic.
Slowly sneak up to the intersection.
Weave slightly in your lane so your headlight has a better chance of being spotted.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the portion of the lane that will bring you into other drivers' fields of vision at the earliest possible moment.
questions.explanation: At a blind intersection, position your motorcycle so oncoming drivers can see you as early as possible. For example, if the blind corner is on your right, ride in the left portion of your lane, not the center.

questions.question: To lessen your chances of an accident, you should:

options.text: Only ride in the afternoon.
Follow the vehicle in front of you as closely as possible.
Not look ahead and focus only on your controls.
Communicate your intentions to other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Communicate your intentions to other drivers.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, stay visible and communicate with other drivers. Use your signals, brake light, and lane position. Keep space around your motorcycle and always scan ahead, behind, and to the sides.

questions.question: A group of riders should pass another vehicle:

options.text: In a staggered formation.
In a pyramid formation.
One at a time.
In a splintered formation.

questions.correctAnswerText: One at a time.
questions.explanation: On a two-lane highway, riders should pass one at a time. The next rider should not pass until the previous rider is safely back in the original lane. Continue this pattern until all riders have passed.

questions.question: When preparing to pass another vehicle on the left, you should:

options.text: Ride in the right portion of the lane.
Ride in the left portion of the lane.
Get as close as possible to the vehicle in front of you.
Not signal your intentions, as that may distract the driver you are passing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the left portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: When passing on the left, ride in the left portion of your lane. Signal your intentions and check for traffic. Pass when safe, then signal and return to your original lane.

questions.question: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield:

options.text: Is not necessary if you have a windshield.
Only protects your eyes.
Helps protect your whole face.
Does not protect your face as well as goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Helps protect your whole face.
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face in a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield is not a substitute for a face shield or goggles.

questions.question: How often should a motorcycle operator check their mirrors?

options.text: Never
Occasionally
Frequently
More often than the amount time spent looking ahead

questions.correctAnswerText: Frequently
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors frequently to know what is behind you and spot potential hazards.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to wobble, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up to get out of the wobble.
Use the brakes slowly.
Hold the handlebars tight and slowly close the throttle.
Shift to a lower gear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handlebars tight and slowly close the throttle.
questions.explanation: Speeding up will make the wobble worse. Instead, hold the handlebars firmly without fighting the wobble. Slowly reduce speed by closing the throttle. Move your weight forward and down. Pull to the side of the road as soon as you can.

questions.question: Riders without helmets are ________ to die in a crash than riders with helmets.

options.text: Half as likely
Twice as likely
Three times as likely
Just as likely

questions.correctAnswerText: Three times as likely
questions.explanation: Riders without helmets are three times more likely to die from head injuries in a crash than riders wearing helmets.

questions.question: What does reflective material on your helmet do?

options.text: Helps other drivers see you.
Is not allowed.
Should only be used at night.
Does not help you be seen.

questions.correctAnswerText: Helps other drivers see you.
questions.explanation: Reflective material on your vest or helmet makes you more visible to other drivers. Use it during the day and at night.

questions.question: To be seen in a driver's rearview mirror ahead of you, where should you ride?

options.text: In the center of your lane.
In the left side of your lane.
In the right side of your lane.
In a weaving pattern.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the center of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane behind a car. This position puts you in their rearview mirror. Drivers check their rearview mirror more often than their side mirrors.

questions.question: How many brakes do most motorcycles have?

options.text: Only a front brake.
Only a rear brake.
Both front and rear brakes.
Three brakes: front, rear, and an emergency brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both front and rear brakes.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycles have two brakes: one for the front wheel and one for the rear wheel.

questions.question: How should you brake on a motorcycle?

options.text: Squeeze the front brake and press the rear brake.
Grab the front brake and squeeze the rear brake.
Jam on the front brake and grab the rear brake.
Press the front brake and jam the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Squeeze the front brake and press the rear brake.
questions.explanation: Squeeze the front brake lever and press down on the rear brake pedal. Always use both brakes when you slow down or stop.

questions.question: How do you lean a motorcycle to turn?

options.text: Press the handgrip toward the direction of the turn.
Press the handgrip away from the direction of the turn.
Apply the front brake.
Apply the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handgrip toward the direction of the turn.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle leans to turn. Press the handgrip in the direction you want to turn.

questions.question: When braking normally, what should you do?

options.text: Use only the front brake.
Use only the rear brake.
Alternate between front and rear brakes to save the brakes.
Always use both the front and rear brakes together.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always use both the front and rear brakes together.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while riding and you must stop, what should you do?

options.text: Loosen your grip on the handlebars.
Shift your weight toward the tire that is still good.
Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
Use both brakes and stop quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
questions.explanation: Hold the handlebars firmly and slow down by easing off the throttle. If you must brake, gradually brake only on the tire that is still good. Edge toward the side of the road, squeeze the clutch, and stop.

questions.question: When riding behind a car, what should you do?

options.text: Stay in a position where the driver can see you.
Always ride in the far left side of your lane.
Do not worry about where you position yourself.
Always ride in the far right side of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in a position where the driver can see you.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane behind a car. This position is most likely to be visible in their rearview mirror. Drivers check their rearview mirror more often than their side mirrors.

questions.question: When transporting a load in a sidecar, you should:

options.text: Let the load move freely.
Secure the load so it does not shift.
Place the load unsecured in the seat.
Secure the load near the front of the sidecar.

questions.correctAnswerText: Secure the load so it does not shift.
questions.explanation: Secure the load in the sidecar so it does not shift and change how the motorcycle handles. Place the load toward the rear of the sidecar to prevent the front from tipping during sharp left turns.

questions.question: As a beginning rider, what following distance should you keep behind another vehicle?

options.text: Keep at least four seconds between you and the other vehicle.
Get as close as possible to the other vehicle.
Do not worry about following distance.
Always ride in the left portion of the lane so drivers can see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep at least four seconds between you and the other vehicle.
questions.explanation: Beginning riders should keep at least four seconds of distance behind other vehicles. Increase this distance if weather or road conditions are poor.

questions.question: Where is a motorcycle most likely to conflict with other traffic?

options.text: Intersections
Highways
Parking lots
Residential areas

questions.correctAnswerText: Intersections
questions.explanation: Intersections have the greatest risk of conflict between motorcycles and other traffic. Stay alert at intersections where another vehicle may pull in front of you.

questions.question: A person is legally intoxicated if their blood alcohol concentration (BAC) is at least ______ percent.
questions.explanation: A BAC of 0.08 percent or higher is legally intoxicated in Kentucky. Never operate a motorcycle while under the influence of alcohol.

questions.question: After mounting your motorcycle, which of the following should you NOT do?

options.text: Make sure the mirrors are clean.
Make sure the horn works.
Close the fuel supply valve.
Make sure the clutch works smoothly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Close the fuel supply valve.
questions.explanation: After mounting your motorcycle, check that the clutch, throttle, horn, and brakes work properly. Clean and adjust the mirrors and keep the fuel supply valve open.
